stem: Before surgery, the nurse reviews the client's ASA Physical Status classification. What does this classification primarily describe?

options.A: The procedural experience of the surgical and anesthesia teams and the technical complexity expected during the operation.
options.B: The insurance-authorization category assigned to the operation and the administrative level of care approved for the admission.
options.C: The client's overall preoperative physiologic status and severity of systemic disease, used as one part of perioperative risk assessment.
options.D: A complete prediction of postoperative outcome based on the planned procedure, anesthesia duration, and operative complexity without other factors.

rationale: StatPearls/NCBI describes the ASA Physical Status Classification as a standardized method for assessing and communicating a surgical patient's underlying physiologic status and extent of systemic disease. It can contribute to perioperative risk stratification, but the source explicitly states that it cannot be used alone to determine anesthesia or surgical risk because factors such as procedure invasiveness, frailty, and other clinical variables also matter. Therefore C is correct. A and B describe unrelated administrative or team factors, and D incorrectly turns ASA status into a complete stand-alone outcome model.
educational_objective: Interpret ASA Physical Status as a classification of preoperative physiologic/systemic-disease burden that contributes to, but does not independently determine, overall perioperative risk.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_document_title: American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Classification System
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; last update February 11, 2025; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Continuing Education Activity/Introduction: standardized assessment of physiologic status and medical comorbidities before surgery; six ordinal categories communicate underlying physiologic status. Introduction/Clinical Significance: ASA cannot be used alone to determine anesthesia/surgical risk; additional procedure and patient factors contribute.
source_claim_supported: ASA Physical Status describes underlying preoperative physiologic/systemic-disease status and is only one component of perioperative risk assessment.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative assessment and interpretation of risk-related findings.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only 'only' wording and made all options parallel descriptions of what the classification might represent.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — NCBI explicitly defines ASA status by systemic disease/physiologic condition and explicitly rejects its use as a complete stand-alone operative-risk model.
